chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the mothers of the children, is it permissible for her to uncover her head in front of the men? He (peace be upon him) said: She should wear a scarf (cover her head).

key_terms.تَقَنَّعُ: She should wear a scarf/cover her head

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a married woman uncovering her head in front of men according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the specific requirement of *taqannu* (wearing a headscarf/veil) for married women, distinguishing their status in the presence of non-mahram men. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on modesty as a mandatory obligation for women of childbearing age, linking physical covering to social dignity and religious identity within the domestic and public spheres.
